observations: A shows a gold lever held by the left person's raised hand, passing beneath an open curved tyre lip at the wheel's upper-left edge. The hooked gold end remains visible below the lip at intended size.
B's upper-left contact forms a more nearly closed dark loop around the lever tip; at 768 pixels wide it can resemble a separate ring attached to the wheel rather than a lifted section of tyre.

In both versions the raised working hand joins the left person's forearm and bent teal sleeve. The supporting palm touches the opposite tyre edge and connects through a distinct forearm to the right person's sleeve.

A shows the brown workbench through the lower spoke spaces, making the removed wheel read as an open wheel standing in front of the bench. B retains a uniformly pale wheel interior across this region.
Both versions preserve inward-facing profiles, a large central wheel, quiet workshop context and clear teal/rust separation between the two collaborators.
The target has an open lifted lip, the same people and palette, and a uniformly pale wheel interior. A follows its contact concept while changing the lower wheel interior to show the bench.

brief.reason: At 768 × 512, two people visibly cooperate on a removed wheel. The gold lever passes beneath a lifted tyre lip, and the opposite hand steadies the tyre. Both hands have plausible separate arm ownership.

composition.reason: The wheel dominates between two inward-facing figures; the gold tool and opposing hand provide a readable repair sequence. Sparse workshop context leaves the action unobstructed.

alignment.reason: The central wheel, bench plane and flanking figures form a stable arrangement. Hand placement supports the opposing roles without unwanted tangencies that obscure ownership.

typography.reason: The brief requests wordless artwork and the illustration contains no text.

color.reason: Dark teal tyre and contours separate clearly from the cream background. Teal and rust shirts distinguish participants, while the gold lever gives the small working detail a useful accent.

style.reason: Flat vector masses, simplified profiles and restrained detail form a coherent editorial language. The minimal faces and workshop objects support the shared action without competing with it.

distinctiveness.reason: The opposing repair roles, raised levering gesture and visible lifted lip give the scene a specific bicycle-repair narrative rather than interchangeable workshop decoration.

craft.reason: Full and use-size renders retain clean silhouettes, legible spokes and distinct hand/tool layers. The bench visible through the lower spoke spaces improves spatial credibility. Anatomy remains stylized but intelligible.

visual_fidelity.reason: A preserves the target's figures, palette, large wheel, gold diagonal lever and open lifted-lip concept. The lip is smaller and shifted relative to the target, and the bench now appears through the lower wheel interior; these departures preserve the intended scene and improve its spatial reading.

copy_assessment.reason: No copy is required or present; the narrative is carried by the illustration.

comparison.reason: A makes a clear net communication improvement: the tyre lift reads as an open lip over the engaged lever instead of B's ringlike contact, and the bench through the spokes makes the wheel's open construction more convincing. People, arm ownership and focal hierarchy remain equally legible.

brief_comparison.reason: Against the common wordless repair brief, A better communicates both meaningful lever engagement and a removed spoked wheel on a workbench. This preference rests on the visible repair narrative at intended size, independently of matching the target.

regression.evidence: No consequential loss is visible relative to B. The reduced lip remains discernible at 768 pixels wide, the gold hook still sits beneath it, both hand-to-arm connections are preserved, and the added bench visibility strengthens the wheel's spatial relationship.

summary: A is the stronger resolved editorial illustration. Its open tyre lip and visible bench through the spokes clarify the repair action while preserving collaboration, arm ownership and the restrained visual style.
